node.osc.packet.name: Build OSC packet
node.osc.packet.description: Build an OSC message without sending it. Supply arguments in port order, one array, or connect an existing message to Original OSC packet. A supplied address overrides the original packet address; otherwise keep it. Integers use i when they fit Int32, otherwise h. Explicit Int64 and tagged h use h even for small values. Argument order and explicit wire types are preserved. Up to 64 arguments; arrays and packets cannot be mixed with other argument inputs.
Choose arguments in message order. Each: Choose arguments in message order. Each argument becomes a separate port. Received types must match; values are never silently converted.
Changing or removing an argument may inv: Changing or removing an argument may invalidate existing connections. Validate the workflow after editing.
OSC address to send. A connected Address: OSC address to send. A connected Address input takes precedence.
Leave empty to receive every OSC address: Leave empty to receive every OSC address, or enter an exact address such as /control/start.
Fix the number, order and types of OSC a: Fix the number, order and types of OSC arguments. Each argument gets its own port. Unset keeps the original packet mode; an empty list means no arguments.
The service node and region determine th: The service node and region determine the endpoint. Use an API key and model from the same region.
Not used with the current selection: Not used with the current selection
node.osc.parse.name: Parse OSC packet
node.osc.parse.description: Parse an OSC packet object or raw OSC bytes without network access. Specify argument types as on OSC receivers to expose individual outputs. Types and counts must match. Unset types preserve packet mode; bundles retain their timetag and structure. Maximum input: 1 MiB.
Supply an OSC packet object or raw OSC b: Supply an OSC packet object or raw OSC bytes.
The OSC packet is malformed, unsupported: The OSC packet is malformed, unsupported or exceeds the 1 MiB limit.
